advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Collapse the two mcp `if` blocks (autodeploy.sh:715/719) into one `if changed_range ...; then if mcp_backoff_active ... else <deploy> fi fi` so the delta is computed once and the backoff branch cannot drift out of complement.
evidence: The bot path at 696-704 uses a single `if changed_range ...; then if bot_backoff_active ...` structure; the mcp path diverges from that idiom, running the git diff twice and duplicating the backoff predicate.
advisory.finding: The mcp block re-evaluates `mcp_backoff_active` and re-runs `changed_range "$mcp_deployed" "$TARGET" "$MCP_PATHS"` (a git diff) across two adjacent, mutually-exclusive `if` statements (lines 715 and 719) instead of one if/else. The two predicates must stay exact logical complements; editing one branch's delta condition without the other would silently create a tick that neither marks incomplete nor deploys (dropping a pending mcp change) or one that does both.
advisory.suggested_fix: Mirror the bot gate: `if changed_range "$mcp_deployed" "$TARGET" "$MCP_PATHS"; then if mcp_backoff_active; then log ...; mcp_incomplete=1; else <deploy body> fi fi`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm it is intended that an mcp-only backoff tick skips the host-observability and certbot re-materialization blocks, or move those idempotent blocks above the incomplete guard so mcp's failure state does not delay unrelated host-probe/cert refreshes.
evidence: The commit message justifies skipping the footer's deployed-sha advance on an incomplete tick, but does not address that the OBS/CERTBOT idempotent re-materialization (documented as non-fatal, staleness-alarmed) is also skipped when only mcp is throttled.
advisory.finding: A tick where only mcp backs off (mcp_incomplete=1) now takes the early `exit 0` at line 826, skipping the host-observability (839) and certbot (862) re-materialization blocks. Previously those blocks were reached whenever the review-bot did not defer. A pending OBS_PATHS/CERTBOT_PATHS change unrelated to mcp is therefore deferred until a tick with no open mcp backoff window, coupling host-probe/cert refresh to mcp's failure state.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting a fully completed deploy tick (bot block a no-op, e.g. only MCP_PATHS changed, bot idle) stamps bot-deployed-sha == $TARGET at the footer.
evidence: search of test file for `bot-deployed-sha`: lines 1113-1115 and 1418-1425 all assert `!= _TARGET` / `not (... == _TARGET)` (absence on incomplete ticks); no assertion that a fully complete deploy tick leaves bot-deployed-sha == _TARGET

The lockstep footer comment states the marker must be stamped when 'every component is genuinely at $TARGET', but no test exercises a tick where the bot block is a no-op (nothing under BOT_PATHS changed) yet the tick completes, which is precisely the case the footer stamp guards.
advisory.finding: The newly added success-footer line that stamps bot-deployed-sha=$TARGET on a COMPLETE deploy (`echo "$TARGET" > "$BOT_SHA_FILE.tmp" && mv "$BOT_SHA_FILE.tmp" "$BOT_SHA_FILE"`) has no positive-case test: all bot-deployed-sha assertions in the suite check ABSENCE on incomplete ticks. A regression removing only the footer stamp (leaving the in-function stamp) would go undetected for the mcp-no-op-but-bot-deployed lockstep case.
scenarios: A later refactor drops the footer bot-deployed-sha stamp; a tick where BOT_PATHS did not change but the deploy completes leaves a stale bot marker, and the suite stays green.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the mcp-deployed-sha marker + mcp delta-gate re-pointing belong to cf34 (not in this trailer) and are not being introduced under 5774.
evidence: 5774 Boundary correction: 'The mcp completion marker (`mcp-deployed-sha` and re-pointing the mcp delta gate to it) has MOVED to `cf34-9b8b-1aa7-4d95`. ... This ticket keeps the BOT-side marker, the scoped backoffs, and the incompleteness flags.'
advisory.finding: The mcp completion marker (MCP_SHA_FILE / mcp-deployed-sha) and the re-pointing of the mcp delta gate to diff from the component marker (mcp_deployed) rather than the global $DEPLOYED baseline appear in this 5774 change, but 5774's own scope explicitly MOVED this to cf34-9b8b-1aa7-4d95, which is not in the commit's rebar-ticket trailer.
advisory.suggested_fix: If cf34 is not co-referenced in the rebar-ticket trailer, add it, or split the mcp-deployed-sha / mcp delta-gate hunks into the cf34 change per 5774's stated boundary.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the deploy_review_bot hoist + bot_deferred/return-not-exit deferral scoping is carried under cf34 (its named ticket), not introduced solely under 5774.
evidence: cf34 Proposed fix: 'HOIST the bot block into a new function `deploy_review_bot`, and have the deferral set `bot_deferred=1` and `return 0` from it. Control then reaches the mcp block.'

cf34 Scope note: the per-component markers/backoff/incompleteness flags were SPLIT OUT to symbiotic-cold-flee (5774); cf34 'is now exactly what it was filed as: scoping the review-bot deferral so control reaches the mcp block.'
advisory.finding: The review-bot deferral restructure — hoisting the bot block into deploy_review_bot() and having the drain gate set bot_deferred=1 and `return 0` instead of `exit 0` so control reaches the mcp block — is present in this 5774 change, but that is cf34-9b8b-1aa7-4d95's entire stated fix and cf34 is not in the commit's rebar-ticket trailer.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add cf34-9b8b-1aa7-4d95 to the rebar-ticket trailer if this commit legitimately delivers both, or move the deferral-scoping hunks to the cf34 change.
